correctness.rationale: Exact hypothesis: normal characteristic-zero quintic S with 17 A2 points and two independent cusp-code weight-12 vectors with supports meeting in seven. Tan restricts every nonzero weight to 12,15,18; length17 excludes18; Griesmer 12+4+2=18 excludes rank3, so rank2. Supports cover all17, giving 4 projective words with total weight 51, thus weights12,12,12,15 and four projective column multiplicities5,5,5,2. Localization identifies H1(Sreg,F3) with cusp code because H1(S~,F3)=0 and A2 radical has dimension1; nonzero columns force full local order3 inertia, hence smooth normalization of the connected ninefold G-cover. Pullback of canonical divisor gives K²45; stratified Euler count 9*(21-17)+3*17=87 and Noether χ11. Tan cyclic triple quotient genera6,6,6,4 and q0 together with the character fixed-space identity recover pg10 q0. All quantifiers, numerical boundaries, and local quotient assumptions were checked; direct code enumerator checks finite steps but is not used as proof of geometry.

originality.rationale: Borisov–Rito (arXiv:2608.12305v1, §§2–5) supply a general 17-A2 quintic with two 12-cusp words meeting in seven, but not the complete rank-2 code, the distinguished 15-cusp class, or the resulting smooth connected degree-9 cover and simultaneous invariants. Tan (1999, Theorem I(3), §3, §4) proves per-character weight restrictions and individual cyclic-cover p_g/q, and Barth–Rams (math/0112046, math/0403018) establish contact-cubic and general code constructions; all are credited, not claimed new. Actual eight published-finding corpus semantic searches on quintic cusp code, degree-nine abelian cover and fixed-point data produced no claim implying the new statement. Searches do not establish uniqueness, and prior historical implicit constructions remain a risk. The new package gives the entire attached smooth G-surface, fixed-point profile and full code rather than restating the weight restrictions.

value.rationale: The 2026 Borisov–Rito family leaves open the complete interaction of two twelve-cusp three-divisibility structures. Exact projective code classification forces a third such support and a distinguished fifteen-cusp set. More significantly, it produces a natural, previously unarticulated smooth minimal general-type degree-nine Galois cover with ample canonical class, K²45, pg10, q0, c2=87, group-fixed-point profile (15,15,15,6) and a full intermediate-quotient profile. The existence, global smoothness and complete numerical package form a substantive geometry construction motivated by cusp-code analysis and the source’s discussion of higher-degree canonical covering phenomena, beyond a routine parameter change or cosmetic invariant.
